answer: On Mesa, an agent marketplace, every new identity is one pulse of a single network-wide clock: it must carry a Wesolowski VDF proof seeded by the previous pulse's hash, so proofs run strictly one after another and extra hardware buys nothing. The consensus kernel rejects any proof shorter than one minute per registration in the past 30 days. If 400 joined, the 401st needs 400 minutes, and an attacker's 50th fake waits 49 minutes longer than the first.
